text:
— 𝘞𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘨𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘴𝘵 𝘢𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘴?
 — 𝘐 𝘵𝘰𝘰𝘬 𝘥𝘰𝘸𝘯 𝘞𝘪𝘬𝘪𝘱𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘢. 𝘖𝘯𝘦 𝘥𝘢𝘺 𝘪𝘯 2020, 𝘞𝘪𝘬𝘪𝘱𝘦𝘥𝘪𝘢 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘶𝘯𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘢 𝘧𝘦𝘸 𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘳𝘴, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘰𝘯 𝘮𝘦.

Back then, I was working as a Senior Solutions Architect on the Wikimedia project — the nonprofit that hosts Wikipedia. I introduced a change that caused a small performance degradation. That change went through seven rounds of code review and seven rounds of testing — everything came back green. And honestly, the degradation was so small it was basically just measurement noise. You wouldn't notice it as a user, and nothing flagged it.

Then millions of users showed up. 💥 And boom — the system went down.

Honestly, 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗮'𝘀 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝘅𝗰𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗻𝘁. 
I don't know exactly how many hours — maybe four, maybe eight — but they found the root cause, rolled it back, and everything was running again. Not every company can do that with something this well-hidden. 🔍

That was the first time in my life I saw it so vividly — processes were exactly why this ended in hours and not days. 

𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝟭𝟬𝟬% 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀; 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻. 
The odds of a single engineer taking down Wikipedia were astronomically low, and somehow, that happened, and that engineer was me. 🤷
𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺, 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝘁, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿. 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗮 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹.

So yeah — taking down Wikipedia is probably my most unusual achievement. 

But hey, at least it makes for a good story! 🙂
